paragraphs.text: We owe future generations at least a world that is no worse than the one we were given. People who are not born yet cannot vote or complain, but that does not make their interests count for less. If anything, they are more vulnerable, because they depend entirely on choices made before they arrive. Their claim on us is like the claim of a stranger in another country: real, even if we never meet them. Most philosophers now accept some version of this view.

paragraphs.text: Think about a city that builds a dam it knows will fail in eighty years. Nobody alive today will be hurt when it fails, but we would still say the builders did something wrong. Engineers who cut corners on purpose would not be excused because their victims were born later, and we would blame them even more if they had simply saved money. The harm is real even though the people harmed do not exist yet; this shows that time alone does not cancel a duty.

paragraphs.text: Parfit's non-identity problem is the strongest objection. Our choices change which people are born, so the people of the future cannot complain that we made them worse off, without our choices they would not exist at all. Parfit himself thought the problem was real and spent years looking for a principle that avoids it. If no particular person is made worse off, it can seem that no one is wronged. I think this objection is clever but it does not change what we should do.

paragraphs.text: Climate policy is the clearest case. Every ton of carbon we burn now makes storms and droughts worse for people a century from now. Sea walls, crop failures and heat waves will fall hardest on people who had no say in our choices. Cutting emissions costs us something today, but the cost to them is much larger. Even a small chance of these harms should count, because so many people will live through them.

items.text: Paragraph 3, reply to Parfit. If a different choice would have meant different people were born, why do I still think we owe future people a duty? Write out my reason and check whether it answers that objection.
Compare the opening claim with the conclusion. What limit on our duty does the conclusion make clear? Check that a reader can tell from the opening what I’m prepared to defend.
Paragraph 1, “Most philosophers.” Can I support that claim with a source I’ve read? If I drop it, what reason can I give the reader for accepting my view?
Paragraph 2, dam example. What did the builders know when they decided to proceed, and how did they know the dam would fail? Make that clear to the reader.
Paragraph 4, climate costs. What measure am I using to call the future cost larger? Choose one concrete comparison and check that I use the same measure for people today and in the future.
Paragraph 3, sentence containing “worse off.” Read it aloud, find where each complete thought ends, and choose the punctuation myself.
Paragraph 5, Parfit citation. Find the passage in the edition I used, check what claim it supports, and enter the page number myself. Monday’s citation suggestion is still pending.
Final check on paragraph 2. Monday’s accepted punctuation suggestion already fixed the comma splice. Revisit the original dam sentence and decide for myself how to punctuate it for the final.

item.text:
I reviewed all eight comments and saved a checklist for Friday’s final draft. Dr. Lindqvist’s Wednesday update allows planning help and asks you to write your own fixes, so the checklist uses questions you can work through.

I put your reply to Parfit first. If different choices would lead to different people being born, why do you think the duty still holds? The other items cover your thesis, the “most philosophers” claim, what the dam builders knew, the climate-cost comparison, and the run-on in paragraph 3.

Monday’s accepted suggestion already fixed the dam paragraph’s comma splice. The checklist flags it for your own punctuation review. The Parfit citation suggestion is still pending, so I included a reminder to verify the page in your copy. The paper is due Friday, March 12 at 11:59 p.m. Eastern.
